Abstract In a world where geopolitical tensions strongly impinge on international scientific collaboration and where some scientific information has significant commercial value, the notion of science and practice of it as a global public good are under pressure and so are the ways to pursue it. Science diplomacy acknowledges that science impacts diplomacy and diplomacy impacts science, and that both cooperation and competition shape the diverse practices of science diplomacy: from science fostering international relations and serving global public goods to foreign and security policy interests conflicting with the notion of science as an open collaborative enterprise.
